title: Open-site transport of module contraction
statement: For a scheme X and open U, a natural internal-Hom comparison e and a unit-normalized symmetric core monoidal structure m on the open-site equivalence, contraction with any module-valued dual input v commutes with transport. The input module W, its map h to the transported dual-input module, and the output map k are arbitrary. No complexes, integer degrees or Hom-complex comparison occur.

source.place: Tag 03EO, tensor-Hom adjunction; open-site reindexing and the scalar naturality argument written in the parent proof; Tags 08DL and 08DQ motivate compatibility with restriction and dual evaluation.

proof.text: For each object T of the thin localized open site, take the free presheaf of modules on the representable yoneda(T). The map sending each basis vector to 1 in the structure presheaf is injective: each representable section set is empty or a singleton. Sheafification preserves this monomorphism, giving a subobject G_T of the tensor unit. For every local section b of a module B, the free-presheaf universal property and the sheafification adjunction give a map G_T to B taking its distinguished section to b. This also works over the zero ring and for empty representable section sets.

Natural transformations from tensorRight(V) to a monomorphism-preserving functor H are determined by their component at the tensor unit. Naturality along G_T to the unit and monicity of its H-image give equality at G_T. Naturality along G_T to B then gives equality on every local pure tensor b tensor v. The presheaf tensor extensionality lemma and the sheafification adjunction give equality on the sheaf tensor product. Apply this with H = internal Hom from A, which preserves monomorphisms since it is a right adjoint.

Define contraction c_B by the displayed tensor-Hom transpose before the final output map k. Prove its naturality in B and in its dual input directly from the tensor-Hom naturality, braiding naturality, associator naturality and right unitor naturality. At the tensor unit, c_unit = leftUnitor(V).hom followed by v, by the unit and symmetry coherence identities.

Put w = L(v) followed by e(A,unit).hom and internal Hom applied to the inverse unit comparison. Compare the natural family c_B with the family obtained by pulling target contraction back through the inverse tensorator and inverse e using fullness of L. Tensorator naturality and he make the latter family natural in B. The families agree at the unit by the preceding unit contraction identity and m.left_unitality. The natural-transformation extensionality result makes them equal for all B; faithfulness and the comparison isomorphisms yield the required core transport equation.

Apply naturality in the dual input to the arbitrary map h and substitute hunit and hv. Use tensor-Hom naturality in the output, he and hk to postcompose with the arbitrary output map k. This gives precisely the unchanged displayed statement. No scalar classification, canonical reindexing comparison, or uniqueness theorem for tensorators is required; the extra symmetry hypothesis is retained in the signature.
